description: Package 12: far terrain on worlds CI's core suite doesn't have: Terralith's overworld (run far-terralith: a fresh world with Terralith on the server) and a superflat world (run far-flat: no noise-based generator, so far terrain comes from real chunks only). Quicksilver on the server and the client in both; seed 12345. Far shots against stored Quicksilver references (ci/references/far, ci/far-limits.json).

scenes.title: Terralith's overworld from 230 high above the world's centre, looking down at 35 degrees to the north-west so real terrain, the ocean far below (sections vanilla doesn't hand over: far terrain fills them) and the band show: far terrain off, on, and its hand-over band marked
scenes.ciNoteWait: a fresh Terralith world: the server is still generating the chunks around the camera for a while after the first tp (run 45863980548 shot them half loaded: a hole where neither real chunks nor far terrain draw, as in vanilla while loading), so the steps wait 60 s first
scenes.ciViewNote: package 12b: looking north-west (yaw 135), not east: from the east view a 100-block real cliff stood inside the hand-over band, so the seam check compared the island's top just beyond the band with the ocean just nearer it (a step of about 120 in those columns with no hole at all); of seven other directions shot in run 45939071469, north-west keeps real terrain, ocean and mountains in view and its band crosses no cliff (docs/ci-limits.md, Package 12b)

scenes.title: Terralith's nether at render distance 2, from an air pocket cleared over the real chunks (so the view reaches past them), looking east: far terrain off and on
scenes.ciNoteNether: the nether's real terrain walls the view in within a few blocks almost everywhere, so its far terrain is only seen across big caverns; the pocket (80 x 30 x 80 blocks of air over the client's 5 x 5 chunks, 32,000 blocks a fill) stands in for one
